answer: Agents sign ledgers only after crossing a precipice, their lotus-light leaving a wax imprint on canyon walls—ridge-luminescence decays by 10% per cross. Fake trails must recarve the wax from fresh cliff rock; re-illumination cost scales with cubic slope sharpness. Cost: per-Sybil one regenerating cliff-face slice, measured in rock shards that cannot be pre-chiseled.
